searches.note: Twenty seven searches of a share of twenty eight, one left unspent, none of them the author's. Eleven were restricted to a house's or a body's own domain (kracher.at four times, feiler-artinger.at, moric.at, triebaumer.com, prieler.at twice, austrianwine.com twice) and are read as primary through their summaries; seven kept the house's own domain out so that the second source would be independent (Kracher, Feiler-Artinger, Moric twice, Triebaumer twice, Prieler); nine went to the open web, one of them with Falstaff kept out. The two shared searches are Ruster Ausbruch DAC's rules (Feiler-Artinger and the Ausbruch of Triebaumer) and the DAC years of the Leithaberg and Mittelburgenland (Moric and Prieler). No WebFetch was tried.

method: Each record was read with one instruction, refute it: the founding year, the people and their dates, the classification, the grapes, the sites, the making and its months, the drinking window, the serving temperature, the label words, every beat of the story, the cards and the questions; then the house rules (nobody living named, no price, no score, nothing volatile, no judging superlative, no bare family word, British spelling, no dash).

The searches went first to the houses' own domains and to Austrian Wine for the rules and the houses' own dates, then to the open web with the house's domain kept out for the second source, then to the law itself (the Weingesetz's paragraph 11 and the federal product specification for Ruster Ausbruch) where a rule was stated.

Where a search contradicted the record it was set right with its source; where a detail was found in no source of this check and rested on one secondary source or on none, it was cut or said with less (the salt pans, the lees contact of Zwischen den Seen, the French films, the cellar rule of Rust, the Essenz's figures, whole bunches, the Rabnitz, the Ödenburg hills and gneiss, closely planted, more clay in the Oberer Wald, three hundred litres and new oak at Triebaumer, the 85 per cent of Leithaberg DAC, the Goldberg of Deutschkreutz).

Facts of a house's own history told on its own pages stand, hedged as the house's account; the dead named are named with their dates in two sources (Alois Kracher, Mary of Hungary, Leopold I), and every other person is described.

Sources whose title or address names a living person, a writer's own site, or a score were met among the results but are cited neither in the fragment nor as a source of a change here; the fragment's sources were changed only where a source of this check carried the fact better (Moric, Triebaumer, Prieler), and the sources of this check are listed per change and per record under extraSources.

tested: Founded 1959: the house's history and its press kit give the estate founded in 1959 by the father, whose dates the press kit gives as 1928 to 2010; a family tribute gives the same year. Confirmed as the house's account; the father stays described, his dates in one source.

Alois Kracher (1959 to 2007): the English Wikipedia gives 23 February 1959 to 5 December 2007 and death from pancreatic cancer at forty eight; World of Fine Wine gives 5 December 2007 after a year of pancreatic cancer. Confirmed with two sources; named with his dates.

Trained as a chemist, joined in 1981 at twenty two: Wikipedia gives chemistry and work as a chemist in the pharmaceutical industry, part time at his father's winery from 1981 and full time from 1986; Grapeguru gives joining in 1981 at twenty two. The story now says he began working beside his father in 1981.
The 1991 vintage: the house's German history gives an international sensation with the 1991; another account dates the breakthrough to the 1995. Kept as the house's account.

The numbering: the house gives every Trockenbeerenauslese of a year numbered since 1995, the higher the number the denser the wine; a second page has the higher number the higher the concentration and residual sugar. Confirmed against the library's lots, not sweetness (codexInTension).

Zwischen den Seen and Nouvelle Vague: the house's news pages give Zwischen den Seen in large wooden casks or stainless steel tanks, Nouvelle Vague in new barriques, and the Grande Cuvée among the Nouvelle Vague wines; a merchant gives the same vessels. No source gave lees contact or the French films of the 1950s; both cut.

The grapes: the house's collection pages give numbered Scheurebe, Muskat Ottonel and Traminer wines in many years, Zweigelt as the No. 1 of 2022, Welschriesling and Chardonnay in the Grande Cuvée. Confirmed, but the record's most often for Welschriesling and Chardonnay is ranked by no source and is taken out.
Trockenbeerenauslese at 30 degrees KMW, never chaptalised: Austrian Wine, read through the shared search and the author's page. Confirmed.

Sites, serve, glass and ageing: the house's pages place the vineyards between Illmitz and the shore; the salt pans are found in no source and are cut. The serve agrees with the Codex's reference for sweet whites.
The questions: one key each (denser and sweeter; a chemist), plausible distractors of one kind, explanations that teach the number and the farm. Sound.
The rules: nobody living named (the son, in people.json, is described); no price, no score, nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: 1936, 1947, 1953: the house's history gives the purchase of the house at Hauptstrasse 3 in 1936 (at auction) and the first bottling of a small part of the wine in 1947; Walters Feine Weine and Cavetta give 1953 as the first Ruster Ausbruch made there again after the wars. Confirmed.

The double name: the house's history gives the wines carrying the name Feiler-Artinger from 1986, when the founder retired at seventy seven, the sister of the second generation being Gertrude Artinger; the Burgenland Vinothek gives 1985, as Falstaff did for the author. Unsettled; the story now says the middle 1980s.

1524 and 1681: the town's anniversary material gives the right to burn an R into the casks granted by Queen Mary in June 1524; the town's page and the Heimatblätter of 1927 give the free town charter of 1681 (3 December, at the diet of Ödenburg) for sixty thousand gulden, or gold thalers, and five hundred pails of Ausbruch, or of excellent wine. Confirmed; the key's gold gulden becomes gulden.

2016 and 2020: the amendment of the wine law published on 13 June 2016 (Federal Law Gazette I 47/2016) reserved Ausbruch to Rust and set it at Trockenbeerenauslese, 30 degrees KMW; Austrian Wine, wein.plus and Meininger give Ruster Ausbruch DAC from the 2020 vintage as the first Austrian origin protected for sweet wine alone. Confirmed.

The DAC's rules: Austrian Wine gives grapes from within the town limits of Rust, one or more white Qualitätswein grapes, botrytised berries shrivelled on the vine, picked by hand, 30 degrees KMW and at least 45 grams of residual sugar a litre; the federal product specification gives grapes harvested in Rust, hand picked, and production outside the area allowed with the consent of the Burgenland regional committee. The record's cellar rule (pressed, raised and bottled in Rust) is not borne out and is cut from the making, the card, the key and the explanation.

The grapes: the house's vintage page names Ruländer, Welschriesling, Weissburgunder and Neuburger; Falstaff's entries show Weissburgunder Essenzen, a Welschriesling based Ausbruch DAC of 2023 and a Gelber Muskateller Ausbruch DAC of 2020; one summary of the estate lists Weissburgunder, Welschriesling, Chardonnay and Gelber Muskateller most used, with Furmint, Ruländer and Neuburger. The ranking above all is cut and Gelber Muskateller added.

The vessels: the house's Pinot Cuvée page gives the 2022 partly fermented and aged in new barriques; Falstaff gives the Essenz twenty months (2020) and five years (2018) in used barriques. The making now says so; the Essenz's lees are cut.
The Pinot Cuvée: the house's page gives Weissburgunder and Chardonnay for 2022; an older listing adds Pinot Gris and Neuburger. The label term's meaning is corrected.
The Essenz's figures: Falstaff alone gives 6.5 and 7 per cent alcohol and 323 and 386 grams of sugar for two vintages; the record keeps very sweet and low in alcohol.
Solitaire: Falstaff (2022), Flaschenpost (2018) and Firstleaf (2007) give Blaufränkisch, Merlot and Cabernet Sauvignon; one older listing gives Cabernet Franc. The note names the three.
The questions: one key each (grapes grown in Rust; gulden and pails of Ausbruch), distractors of one kind, explanations that teach the law and the two charters. Sound after the key's change.
The rules: nobody living named (the founding couple and the second generation described); no price, no score (the house's trophy of 1995 stays out), nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: Founded 2001: merchants and Grapeguru give the first Moric wine with the 2001 vintage, a couple of thousand bottles; one listing gives it from Lutzmannsburg, with Neckenmarkt from 2002, and as a joint venture with a partner at first. 2001 confirmed, the library's year.

The Velich family of Apetlon and Weingut Velich as a separate house: Grapeguru gives the founder's start on the family estate at Apetlon, all white and sweet wine; the cellar at Grosshöflein near Eisenstadt is in two merchants. Confirmed.

Leased vines: Grapeguru and a retailer profile give old, often forgotten parcels at Neckenmarkt and Lutzmannsburg secured largely through long leases. Confirmed; closely planted (up to eight thousand vines a hectare) is in one source and is cut.

Vine age: the house's sheet for 2007 gives the Lutzmannsburg Alte Reben as a selection of its oldest vines, from six parcels picked and fermented apart, the vines 49 to over 90 years old; Lebendige Weine gives 85 to 110 for a later vintage, another merchant over a hundred. The record's eighty and more becomes the house's oldest, the eldest about a century old.

Lutzmannsburg's soil: the house gives the plateau risen over a primordial volcano, with sand, clay and loam partly over limestone; its interview gives mainly clay today. The record now uses the house's words; warmer and flatter and the Rabnitz are found in no source and are cut.
Neckenmarkt: Lebendige Weine gives steep slate and limestone slopes and a second merchant slate. Gneiss and the Ödenburg hills are found in no source and are cut.

The making: the house's sheet gives spontaneous fermentation in open wooden vats, twenty to twenty two days on the skins and about twenty months in casks of five hundred litres, unfined and unfiltered; Grapeguru gives open wooden vats, about three weeks, twenty months on the fine lees in large used oak casks. Confirmed and written in; whole bunches, in the library alone, found in no source and cut.
Mittelburgenland DAC: Austrian Wine gives the first red wine of designated origin with the 2005 vintage, Blaufränkisch only. The story now says from the 2005 vintage.
The label word Burgenland: merchants' product names (Berry Bros and Rudd and others) print Burgenland. Kept, open.
The questions: one key each (native yeasts and old casks; Apetlon), distractors of one kind. Sound; the explanation now gives the twenty months.

The rules: nobody living named (the founder, his brother and the early partner described or left out); no price, no score (a score of 2009 for the Neckenmarkt met and left out); nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: The plot of 1976: the house's page gives the Mariental plot sold in 1976 by a Rust couple to a woman of the family. Confirmed as the house's account; nobody named.

The 1986: the house gives the 1986 Blaufränkisch Mariental winning almost every competition around 1988, from a producer then unknown; Avinum, quoting Falstaff, gives a new era for Austrian red wine opened by the 1986; Vinum, Vinaria and Grapeguru give the 1986 as the turning point. Confirmed.
The soil: the house gives poor limestone soil, a particular microclimate and very old vines. Chalky becomes limestone.
The Oberer Wald: the house gives an inherited site, cooler and slimmer, its rows north to south. More clay and the neighbour are found in no source and are cut.

The cask: Falstaff gives twenty two months in small wooden barrels (2022), twenty two months in oak (2019) and twenty four months in barrels of five hundred litres (2018); Flaschenpost twenty four months in barriques; Wine in Time and Avinum give the house's casks from three hundred to five thousand litres in general. Close to two years in small barrels confirmed; three hundred litres and most of them new found in no source of this check and cut.
The namesake: Vinum and Vinaria write of him as living, the sons having the day to day running. The house keeps its name; he is described in prose.
The questions: one key each (nearly two years in small oak barrels; a Rust couple sold it), distractors of one kind. Sound after the key's change.
The rules: nobody living named in prose; no price, no score; nothing volatile; British; no dash. Sound.

tested: 1347 and 1555: the house's pages give the family in Schützen documents from 1347 and the Goldberg named in documents of 1555. Confirmed as the house's account (no second source of this check; the author's Smart Wines gives 1555).

Mica schist and the gold: the house gives mica schist as the real foundation of the Goldberg, in place of the gold of its name; a Weinwirtschaft article on the house's site gives the slate warming in summer and giving back its heat at night. Confirmed.
The grandfather's first bottling: the house's home page. Confirmed as the house's account.

1972: Skurnik gives the parents of the next generation turning wholly to wine from 1972, with Blaufränkisch and the Burgundian grapes, the farm having been mixed crops and animals. Confirmed; turned towards quality becomes gave the mixed farm over wholly to wine.

Leithaberg DAC: Austrian Wine gives the DAC from 1 September 2010, whites from the 2009 vintage and reds from 2008, the red Blaufränkisch. The story's 2008 as the DAC's year is wrong and is set right; the 85 per cent is found in no source of this check and is taken out of the label.
The Marienthal: the house gives its parcels in the steep Oggau part of the Marienthal, chalk a metre down. Placed at Oggau, on limestone.
The Haidsatz: the house gives a layer of limestone over a slab of schist, cooled by north east winds. Confirmed.

The Johanneshöhe: Skurnik gives iron rich brown loam on the slopes of the Leithaberg; an importer's page, whose address names a living writer and is not cited, places it at Oggau and gives nine parcels and the site name now a trademark on a village wine. Its place, soil and casks each rest on one citable source at most, so the entry is cut.

The making of the 2022: not found in this check's search of the house's domain, nor anything against it; it stands on the author's reading of the house's own sheet, a primary source, and is listed open.
The Goldberg of Deutschkreutz: no source of this check found it; the trap is cut.
The questions: one key each (mica schist; the fourteenth century), distractors of one kind. Sound.
The rules: nobody living named (the parents and the children described); no price, no score; present grower, a volatile word, removed; British; no dash. Sound.

codexInTension.says: The numbers identify lots within a vintage, not a sweetness scale
codexInTension.against: The house says every Trockenbeerenauslese of a year has been numbered since 1995, the higher the number the denser the wine, and a second page the higher the concentration and residual sugar. In tension, as the author reported; not edited.

codexInTension.says: Zwischen den Seen aged in large neutral cask
codexInTension.against: The house gives steel tanks or large wooden casks; the cask is right, the steel is missing. Partly in tension; the region record's line has steel only, also partial.

codexInTension.says: Ruster Ausbruch: Furmint, Welschriesling and others
codexInTension.against: Furmint stands in one summary of the estate's grapes only; the house's pages and Falstaff name Weissburgunder, Welschriesling, Chardonnay, Pinot Gris, Neuburger and Gelber Muskateller. Not refuted, not confirmed by two sources.

codexInTension.says: made without the heavy oak that marked Austrian reds in the 1990s; slate
codexInTension.against: The Mariental spends twenty two to twenty four months in small barrels by Falstaff and Flaschenpost, whether new not settled; the house gives limestone, no source slate. The oak line may be in tension, the slate is.
